paper_title: High-Efficiency Polymer Solar Cells Enabled by Environment-Friendly Single-Solvent Processing
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Advanced Energy Materials - 2016 - Zhang - High‐Efficiency Polymer Solar Cells Enabled by Environment‐Friendly/auto/Advanced Energy Materials - 2016 - Zhang - High‐Efficiency Polymer Solar Cells Enabled by Environment‐Friendly.md

knowledge_points.content: 2-methylanisole (MA) is introduced as a nonhalogenated, biodegradable, and low-toxicity single solvent for fabricating polymer solar cells without the need for high-boiling-point additives or post-treatments like thermal annealing.
knowledge_points.evidence: In this work, we first proposed a novel solvent, 2-methylanisole (MA), as the processing solvent to fabricate PSCs... without using any additives or posttreatments. More importantly, MA is a nonhalogenated, biodegradable chemical with low toxicity.

knowledge_points.content: A polymer solar cell based on PBDT-TS1:PC71BM processed with 2-methylanisole (MA) achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 9.67%, with a Voc of 0.79 V, Jsc of 17.39 mA/cm², and FF of 0.704.
knowledge_points.evidence: The PSC device fabricated from MA exhibits an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.79 V, a short-circuit current (Jsc) of 17.39 mA cm−2, a fill factor (FF) of 0.704, and an overall PCE of 9.67%.

knowledge_points.content: The molecular aggregation of the polymer donor in solution, indicated by a shoulder peak in UV-vis absorption spectra at long wavelengths, dictates the final morphology of the bulk-heterojunction blend.
knowledge_points.evidence: The shoulder peak in the long wavelength is attributed to the aggregations of the polymer chains... the comparison among the absorption spectra of the solutions indicates that the aggregation effect of the polymer in MA is slightly stronger than in xylene but obviously weaker than in DCB.

knowledge_points.content: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) reveal that xylene-processed PBDT-TS1:PC71BM films exhibit severe phase separation with PC71BM domains reaching hundreds of nanometers and a root mean square roughness (Rq) of 18.5 nm.
knowledge_points.evidence: the blend film processed by xylene shows sever phase separation and very large domain size; PC71BM forms huge spheres with hundreds of nanometers in diameter... and also the root mean square roughness (Rq) reaches 18.5 nm.

knowledge_points.content: Moderate inter-chain interaction in 2-methylanisole (MA) allows PC71BM domains to grow within a confined polymer network, resulting in an ideal nanoscale phase separation compared to the excessive aggregation in xylene or the overly uniform morphology in DCB.
knowledge_points.evidence: the inter-chain interaction in the MA-processed solution is moderate, so the fullerene domains can grow up in a confined polymer network. Hence, the ideal phase separation morphology can be achieved by using MA as the processing solvent.

knowledge_points.content: The exciton dissociation efficiency (Pdiss) for PBDT-TS1:PC71BM devices processed with 2-methylanisole (MA) is approximately 89.2%, which is determined by the ratio of photocurrent density (Jph) to saturated current density (Jsat).
knowledge_points.evidence: The Jsat of 19.52 mA cm−2 and Pdiss of ≈90% exhibited in MA processed devices are similar to the data acquired from binary-solvent system... (Table 1: MA Pdiss is 89.2%)

knowledge_points.content: Photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy indicates efficient charge separation in MA-processed films through full quenching of the polymer emission peak at 750 nm, whereas xylene-processed films show poor quenching due to excessive phase separation.
knowledge_points.evidence: In the DCB- and MA-processed films, the polymers are well mixed with PC71BM and hence the PL can be fully quenched, which indicates the efficient charge separation process. The xylene-processed film possesses severe phase separation, which is unfavorable for exciton quenching.

knowledge_points.content: The 2-methylanisole (MA) processing method demonstrates a high tolerance for film thickness variations, which is a critical advantage for large-area printing technologies.
knowledge_points.evidence: the efficiencies of MA-processed devices exhibited considerable tolerance of the film thickness (see Figure S1 and Table S1, Supporting Information), which is another advantage for large-area printing technologies.

knowledge_points.content: The efficiency of MA-processed PBDT-TS1 devices (9.67%) is comparable to optimized devices using halogenated binary solvents such as DCB:DIO (9.48%) or non-halogenated binary solvents like xylene:NMP (9.47%).
PBDT-TS1 is a low bandgap copolymer derivative based on benzo[1,2-b:4,5-b']dithiophene (BDT) and thieno[3,4-b]thiophene (TT) units, specifically designed for high-efficiency polymer solar cells.
knowledge_points.evidence: Low bandgap copolymers based on benzo[1,2-b:4,5-b']dithiophene (BDT) and thieno[3,4-b]thiophene (TT) units, namely PBDTTTs... PBDT-TS1, a derivative of PBDTTTs.

knowledge_points.content: 2-methylanisole (MA) is significantly safer for industrial mass production than chlorobenzene (CB) or dichlorobenzene (DCB) because it has only one identified hazard on the Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS).
knowledge_points.evidence: MA is a nonhalogenated, biodegradable chemical with low toxicity, and much safer than CB or DCB for mass production... according to the hazards identification on the Material Safety Data Sheet, there is only one hazard.
